title: Compact generalized rays and uniform observation
source_hypothesis: One fixed normalized scalar second-order differential family on a halfspace with positive tangential dimension, smooth coefficient parameters, real quadratic principal form and complex lower coefficients. Original Banach embedding, actual smooth zero-Dirichlet inputs, compact full target microsupport and bounded complete auxiliary target families. Every maximal normalized generalized ray of the base operator meeting the target cone must meet the observation cone.
reviewed_arguments: H0–H1 retain the fixed normalized scalar halfspace chart, positive tangential dimension, smooth coefficient parameters, complex lower terms, original Banach norm, actual zero trace and bounded full auxiliary target families. Every permitted maximal continuation and stationary normalized ray is included.
G0 applies the proved compact-access theorem before choosing any target order. A compact parameter ball lies strictly inside its validity neighborhood and contains every parameter limit used later.

R0 constructs the full finite elliptic comparison by complete inverses, retaining all proper, partition and low-frequency residuals. R1 controls each particular bounded residual family by its actual admissible source tree and a fixed scalar residual source test.

T0 constructs countably many nested phase neighborhoods and actual full elliptic tests at every nonnegative integer order. T1 checks all local regimes, including strict diffraction with stationary projected boundary field, and uses the complete glancing source list before replacing its final scalar assembly.

T2 gives an explicit countable-subcover argument in parameter-phase space for every finite basis union of observation neighborhoods. The selected estimates preserve every open cap/window implication, with one output neighborhood at all orders.

T3 closes that selected list under every finite elliptic comparison needed for its actual observation operators and the given bounded target families. Every resulting residual source operator is recorded before the countersequence is chosen. No dense-symbol approximation or countable bounded exhaustion of all residual kernels is asserted.

D0 normalizes a sequence on failure of every finite estimate. Compact parameter convergence and a dyadic tail give square summability for each fixed listed datum, without a uniform bound over all data indices.

D1 defines an open regular set by all integer orders on the same nested neighborhood. The complementary closed defect avoids the observation cone and meets the target compact set, by the pre-recorded full target comparisons.

D2 transfers each selected estimate to the defect set using the actual finite comparison of its observation operator. T2 then transfers every admissible open implication. Each order uses a separate finite inequality; an order-independent bound on all constants is unnecessary.

P0 excludes noncharacteristic points and proves compactness of characteristic lifts, retaining both roots at a hyperbolic boundary point. P1 verifies the ordinary, reflected and strict-diffractive segment hypotheses directly for this closed set.

P2 uses the full closed incoming window and its outer band, with both lifts and strict margins. Choosing its width proportional to the signed time produces the precise reduced directional witnesses of the closed-set trajectory theorem, uniformly on compact nonradial glancing anchor sets.

P3 applies that geometric theorem only after its closed-set hypotheses are verified. Signed root recovery, high-contact joining, stationary radial/zero-field exceptions and finite endpoint continuation produce a maximal generalized ray in the defect. Uniform compact access contradicts its avoidance of the observation cone.

C0 proves the actual tested graph completion is injective in the original Banach space by full flat-test transposition, identifies the limiting tests, and preserves a continuous Banach trace when available. No larger-domain density claim is inferred.

Three complete solutions compute exact diagonal tails, show why a dense set of tests does not pass series bounds to a limit, and verify explicit compact access for flat-wave rays including reflection and gliding.

All sixteen current captures were actually inspected: thirteen overlapping desktop sections, the original figure and two mobile samples. The figure plots exact series entries and partial sums, with explicit interpretation; all 290 formulas and 25 displays render.

The result is the fixed-chart all-regime assembly. General manifold coordinate/scalar assembly, any remaining zero-dimensional boundary case, the wave application, sharp Airy mapping and the remaining full course stay active. Human foundation dependencies remain external to the CC0 export.
